ThingDef.label: saved barley seed
ThingDef.description: Barley seed from your own harvest. Sow it instead of buying stock and the line may slowly take to this soil — a little more yield, frost, or dry-spell grit, depending on what the plants survived. The quality stays on the seed; there is nothing to manage.

ThingDef.label: saved pumpkin seed
ThingDef.description: Pumpkin seed from your own harvest. Replant your stock and the vines slowly adapt to this patch of dirt.

ThingDef.label: saved herb seed
ThingDef.description: Herb seed from your own bushes. Keep replanting your stock and the line becomes yours.

ThingDef.label: saved sugar beet seed
ThingDef.description: Sugar beet seed from your own harvest. Replant it and the roots slowly take to this ground.

ThingDef.label: saved flax seed
ThingDef.description: Flax seed from your own harvest. Keep sowing your stock and the fiber line adapts to the homestead.
